Blocking\n// only splits that ascending k range into consecutive chunks that are added into the\n// same running accumulator, so the results are bit-for-bit identical to the original.\n\nnamespace {\n\nconstexpr size_t BS = 32;   // width of a column panel (number of columns per block)\nconstexpr size_t KBB = 256; // k-blocking factor for the trailing-matrix update\nconstexpr size_t TI = 8;    // rows per tile in the update phase\n\n} // namespace\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order\n    if (n == 0) {\n        return true;\n    }\n\n    // P: panel of the current block, transposed and packed as P[k * BS + jj] = L[J + jj][k].\n    // The transposed layout makes the innermost loop of the update a contiguous, and hence\n    // vectorizable, update of BS independent accumulators.\n    std::vector<double> P(n * BS);\n    // ACC[i * BS + jj] holds sum_{k < J} L[i][k] * L[J + jj][k], i.e. the part of the dot\n    // product that has already been accumulated for the current block (zero for J == 0).\n    std::vector<double> ACC(n * BS, 0.0);\n\n    for (size_t J = 0; Blocking\n// only splits that ascending k range into consecutive chunks that are added into the\n// same running accumulator, so the results are bit-for-bit identical to the original.\n\nnamespace {\n\nconstexpr size_t BS = 32;   // width of a column panel (number of columns per block)\nconstexpr size_t KBB = 96;  // k-blocking factor for the trailing-matrix update\nconstexpr size_t TI = 4;    // rows per tile in the update phase\n\n// The scalar reduction \"for (k) sum += a[k] * b[k];\" of the original code is compiled\n// (-O3 -march=native) into groups of four separately rounded products that are added\n// into the accumulator one after another, plus a fused multiply-add for the remaining\n// len % 4 elements. Blocking only splits that ascending range into consecutive chunks added into the same running accumulator, so results stay bit-identical (a right-looking/outer-product update would change the rounding).\n- **Panel loop** (32 columns per panel) runs inside **one persistent parallel region**; phases are separated by barriers instead of opening a new region per phase (this alone took n=1024 @256 threads from 3 → 89 GFLOPS).\n  - *Pack*: blocked transpose of the already-computed panel rows into a cache-friendly layout.\n  - *Update (the bulk of the flops)*: parallel over row tiles, k-blocked so the packed panel stays L1-resident; 32 independent accumulator chains per row, vectorized over columns (8 YMM accumulators) — AVX2 without any reassociation.\n  - *Diagonal block*: serial (it carries the dependencies), a few thousand flops per panel.\n  - *Trailing rows*: independent per row, 4 rows at a time for instruction-level parallelism.\n- **Bit-exact rounding:** GCC compiles the original dot products into four separately-rounded products added serially plus `vfmadd` for the last `len % 4` elements. The kernels reproduce that pattern explicitly, with `-ffp-contract=off` in CMake and `std::fma` for the tail. Generation (`B·Bᵀ`) and validation were parallelized the same way (plus symmetry, halving their work).\n- **Runtime setup:** threads are pinned to the CPUs in the process's affinity mask (barrier cost at 256 threads drops from 1.8 ms to 30 µs; skipped if you set `OMP_PROC_BIND`/`GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY`), the matrix pages are first-touched round-robin for NUMA spread, and for small matrices the thread count is capped to what can be kept busy (never above `OMP_NUM_THREADS`).\n\n**`cholesky/CMakeLists.txt`** — `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)`, link `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX`, add `-ffp-contract=off` (commented).
